ns2:group.ns2:title: China Unveils Waterproof Robotic Hand That Works From the Kitchen to the Mariana Trench
ns2:group.ns2:description:
A Chinese startup has introduced the world’s first waterproof dexterous robotic hand, the WA series, enabling robots to operate in environments ranging from everyday household settings to the deep sea.
The IP68 version handles routine tasks like washing dishes and preparing food, while a deep-sea engineering model can be customized to withstand pressures at depths from 300 to 10,000 meters—deep enough to operate in the Mariana Trench.
The technology opens the door to full-scenario robotic applications, from daily life to extreme environments.

Resale prices for Pop Mart’s Labubu blind boxes have fallen sharply.
The fourth-generation Mini Labubu series sold out instantly when it launched online on August 28, briefly pushing full-box prices on secondary platforms to as high as 1,600 yuan. By late December, those prices had dropped to about 1,077 yuan.

ns2:group.ns2:description:
On December 28, Zhu Jiangming, founder, chairman and CEO of Leapmotor, looked back on the company’s decade-long journey, describing it as “A Near-Death Struggle”.
He said the past ten years were extremely tough and that Leapmotor has only recently moved past the break-even point, after years of operating under intense pressure.
So far, Leapmotor has delivered a total of 1.2 million vehicles. Sales in 2025 are expected to reach nearly 600,000 units.
The company now has more than 1,800 sales and service outlets worldwide, including over 800 overseas.

ns2:group.ns2:description:
In the mid-1980s, Nintendo pretty much ruled the video game industry. And somehow, a few toymakers and inventors convinced Nintendo that the controller of the future was… this big, clunky thing you wore on your right arm. (Sorry, lefties.) It wasn’t very good, but people loved it anyway. And while the Power Glove wasn’t exactly the future of anything, you could argue it helped start a revolution in virtual reality and motion controls. On this episode of Version History, David Pierce, Chris Grant, and Game File’s Stephen Totilo do just that. #VersionHistory #Podcast #Gaming
